code: const ElfW(Nhdr)* const nhdr = reinterpret_cast<const ElfW(Nhdr)*>(note);
note: Attacker-controlled PT_NOTE bytes are interpreted as an ElfW(Nhdr); n_namesz, n_descsz and n_type are taken directly from the raw input.
With n_namesz=4 and align=4, desc_start = (12+4+3) & ~3 = 16; the descriptor is assumed to start 16 bytes into the note.

Integer overflow: with n_descsz=0xFFFFFFFB the aligned descriptor term is 0xFFFFFFFC, and desc_start(16) + 0xFFFFFFFC wraps the 32-bit ElfW(Word) sum to size=12. The size addition is not range-checked before being used.
The overflow guard only rejects n_descsz >= 0xFFFFFFFC; n_descsz=0xFFFFFFFB passes even though (n_descsz+3)&~3 = 0xFFFFFFFC makes the derived size computation wrap.
The wrapped size=12 satisfies both bounds guards (12 >= 12 and note+12 <= last), so the corrupt note is accepted instead of breaking.
BytesToHexString reads n_descsz=0xFFFFFFFB bytes starting at note+desc_start (note+16); the descriptor is far beyond the PT_NOTE buffer, causing an out-of-bounds heap read.
